en: At dawn, I remember the lotus-face of the Lord of the Raghus,
with its gentle smile, sweet speech, and broad forehead;
its cheeks graced by earrings that dangle down to the ears.
With eyes as long as the tips of his ears, he was a delight to the eyes. || 1 ||
In the morning, I worship the lotus-feet of the Lord of the Raghus,
who bestows boons upon his own people and strikes fear into the hosts of Rākṣasas;
he who, in the assembly of kings, broke apart the bow of Maheśa.
He immediately attained the auspiciousness of taking Sītā’s hand in marriage.
At dawn, I bow to the lotus-feet of Raghunātha,
which bear auspicious lines such as the thunderbolt and the goad, which bring me happiness,
and which are served by the honey-bees of the minds of the lords of yogis.
It instantly removed the curse of Gautama’s lawful wife. || 3 ||
In the morning, I utter with my voice the name of Raghunātha;
it removes the defects of speech and destroys all impurity—
that name which Pārvatī, desiring to eat together with her husband, [uttered].
With joy, he recited the thousand names of Hari an equal number of times.
At dawn, I take refuge in the form of Raghunātha, praised by the Vedas,
whose complexion is like a blue lotus, a water-lily, and various other gems including sapphires,
and who is enriched with ornaments of exquisite pearls.
She who is the object of meditation for all sages and the cause of liberation for living beings.
That man who, having awakened at the time of dawn, recites these five verses with devotion every day,
shall indeed become the foremost among the servants of Śrī Rāma.
Having become so, he goes to the realm of Hari, which is unattainable by others.
Thus ends the "Morning Remembrance of Śrī Rāma."
